research_mode: official MHCLG and GOV.UK Residential PEEPs guidance only; scope, relevant-resident, representative and engagement methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Residential PEEPs purpose
verified_claims: The Regulations aim to improve fire safety and evacuation for residents of specified English residential buildings who would have difficulty evacuating without assistance.
limitations: The general purpose does not establish that a particular resident or building is in scope.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Residential PEEPs commencement
verified_claims: The Fire Safety (Residential Evacuation Plans) (England) Regulations 2025 came into force on 6 April 2026.
limitations: Commencement does not prove compliance by an individual responsible person.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: High-rise scope threshold
verified_claims: The Regulations apply to multi-residential buildings in England that are at least 18 metres high or at least 7 storeys.
limitations: Height, storey count and residential use require building-specific evidence.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Over-11-metre simultaneous-evacuation scope
verified_claims: The Regulations also apply to multi-residential buildings over 11 metres that have a simultaneous evacuation strategy.
limitations: The strategy must not be inferred from building height or appearance.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Relevant-resident definition
verified_claims: A relevant resident has the premises as their only or principal residence and would have difficulty evacuating without assistance because of a physical, sensory or cognitive condition.
limitations: Relevant-resident status requires individual and residence-specific assessment.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Reasonable endeavours to identify residents
verified_claims: Responsible persons must use reasonable endeavours to identify relevant residents.
limitations: The guidance does not prescribe one universally sufficient identification method.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Resident-identification cycle
verified_claims: Identification activity should occur when a resident moves in, every 12 months and when an individual approaches the responsible person.
limitations: These opportunities do not prove that every relevant resident was reached.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Voluntary resident participation
verified_claims: A resident decides whether to participate and cannot be compelled to engage with the Residential PEEPs process.
limitations: Voluntary participation does not remove the responsible person's identification and offer duties.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Non-participation and contact records
verified_claims: The guidance recommends recording decisions, declined engagement and cases where reasonable contact efforts did not succeed.
limitations: A record does not by itself prove that contact efforts were reasonable.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Representatives for residents under 18
verified_claims: A representative or person with parental responsibility may engage on behalf of a relevant resident under 18.
limitations: Authority and parental responsibility must be verified in the individual case.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Representatives for adults with cognitive conditions
verified_claims: A qualifying attorney or Court of Protection deputy may assist an adult who cannot engage because of a cognitive condition.
limitations: A cognitive condition does not automatically establish incapacity or representative authority.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Representative instruction scope
verified_claims: A representative may request an assessment, discuss measures and costs, agree an evacuation approach, consent to information sharing and request review.
limitations: The representative's authority is limited to the circumstances and legal basis described in the guidance.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Trusted-person engagement
verified_claims: A cognitively able resident may delegate engagement to a trusted person if the resident is present during the engagement.
limitations: A trusted person is not automatically a legal representative.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Resident final agreement and consent
verified_claims: The resident must ultimately agree measures and the evacuation statement and explicitly consent before relevant information is shared with the Fire and Rescue Authority.
limitations: Agreement must not be inferred from participation or a third party's statement.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Coordination with care providers
verified_claims: Responsible persons are encouraged to coordinate with known care providers or support staff to avoid overlap and ensure appropriate support.
limitations: Coordination requires lawful information sharing and does not transfer statutory duties.
